title: Scope reduction — Cloud platform
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's dive into our cloud platform discussion. We've been considering AWS Enterprise, Azure Essentials, and Google Cloud Platform.

SRE: I'd like to voice a concern about the scalability of the Essentials tier on AWS. We might hit some limits there.

Finance Partner: Understood, but let's remember the substantial cost of AWS Enterprise ($320k/yr) versus Azure Essentials ($120k/yr) and Google Cloud Platform Premium Tier ($260k/yr).

CTO: Speaking of costs, we should also consider the potential expense of migrations, especially if we go with Azure. That could take up to 6 months and risk missing the regulatory deadline.

Platform Engineering Lead: True, and our internal expertise is limited on Google Cloud Platform. Extensive training and onboarding would be required to focus on their Premium Tier services.

Finance Partner: So, it seems like we're leaning towards AWS, but let's not forget AWS Essentials is more affordable at $160k/yr. Plus, our team is more familiar with AWS, reducing initial setup and maintenance time.

CTO: Agreed, but AWS Essentials can't meet regulatory compliance requirements, right? We need to verify that before making a decision.

Platform Engineering Lead: You're correct. We'll need to conduct a 3-month compliance audit and assessment at an additional cost of $16k.

Finance Partner: I suppose that's a reasonable cost, considering the benefits. But, let's remember the scalability concern the SRE raised about the Essentials tier.

SRE: I understand the benefits of AWS, but I'm still worried about potential issues with the Essentials tier's scalability.

Platform Engineering Lead: I appreciate your concerns, SRE. We'll have to plan for potential upgrades to the Premium tier as needed, providing flexibility for future needs.

CTO: Alright, it seems we've reached a decision. Let's implement AWS as our cloud platform, starting with the Essentials tier. We'll upgrade to the Premium tier if necessary, and review AWS Essentials' ability to meet regulatory compliance requirements.

Finance Partner: That sounds like a good plan. But, no one has explicitly signed off on this decision yet.

Platform Engineering Lead: You're right, Finance Partner. I'll make sure to gather everyone's approval and get back to you with the official sign-off.

(Off-topic exchange)

SRE: By the way, have we figured out when the company picnic is this year?

Platform Engineering Lead: I believe HR is still working on that. I'll ask them to let us know as soon as possible.

(Back to the topic)

CTO: Alright, let's move forward with our cloud platform plan. Platform Engineering Lead, I trust you'll oversee the implementation and ensure a smooth transition.

Platform Engineering Lead: Absolutely, CTO. I'll make sure everything gets done efficiently.

Title: Cloud Platform Decision - AWS Essentials

Decision: The team has elected to implement AWS as the cloud platform, starting with the Essentials tier due to cost-effectiveness and familiarity with the system. This decision allows for future flexibility, as the tier can be upgraded to the Premium tier as necessary. There will be an initial 3-month compliance audit and assessment at an additional cost of $16k. The choice was made following considerations of both cost and internal expertise, while acknowledging the need for a review of AWS Essentials' compliance with regulatory requirements.
